document_title: Same pole. Two councils. Texas cities decide on Flock cameras
_note: Slide strings set from the storyboard dossiers and the copywriter pass; each carries its claim ids.
caption:
League City answers on November 3rd.

In 2023 the Legislature added $1 to Texans' auto insurance. A state agency turned the fee into at least 3,200 Flock cameras. In late August the Governor ordered the funding paused. It came as scrutiny over the "AI-powered surveillance devices" mounted, the Tribune reported.

At least 14 cities and counties have since shut off more than 900 Flock cameras, the Tribune reported. El Paso voted on a 60 day clock for its fixed Flock cameras and passed it as revised. Leander stopped "in response to community concerns". Kyle kept its contract 6 to 1. College Station kept its cameras 4 to 2. Laredo asks voters in May.

League City called a nonbinding vote on August 11th, before the pause. Its ballot asks if police should keep the fixed cameras. What will a voter who drives past one say on November 3rd?

#LeagueCity #FlockSafety #ElPaso

S1.headline: The state paused paying for this.
S1.body: A $1 fee added to Texas auto insurance in 2023 helped build the state's Flock network. In late August Governor Abbott ordered agencies to pause that funding as scrutiny over the "AI-powered surveillance devices" mounted, the Tribune reported.
strings: The state paused paying for this.

A $1 fee added to Texas auto insurance in 2023 helped build the state's Flock network. In late August Governor Abbott ordered agencies to pause that funding as scrutiny over the "AI-powered surveillance devices" mounted, the Tribune reported.

S2.headline: It runs on sunlight and a cell signal.
S2.body: College Station says the camera photographs the rear of passing vehicles by day and by night. It sorts each one by make, model and color so the data can be searched.
strings: It runs on sunlight and a cell signal.
College Station says the camera photographs the rear of passing vehicles by day and by night. It sorts each one by make, model and color so the data can be searched.

S3.headline: One dollar. At least 3,200 cameras.
S3.body: A Tribune analysis found the Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Authority put at least $30 million of the fee toward the state's Flock network.
strings: A Tribune analysis found the Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Authority put at least $30 million of the fee toward the state's Flock network.

S4.headline: At least 14 cities and counties shut cameras off.
S4.body: More than 900 Flock cameras went dark after the state money was rescinded in late August. Plano, Robinson and Kendall County ended their contracts.
strings: At least 14 cities and counties shut cameras off.
More than 900 Flock cameras went dark after the state money was rescinded in late August. Plano, Robinson and Kendall County ended their contracts.

S5.headline: El Paso voted on a 60 day clock.
S5.body: As filed, the item called for removing every Flock fixed camera under city control within 60 days. The council passed it as revised on September 15th.
strings: El Paso voted on a 60 day clock.
As filed, the item called for removing every Flock fixed camera under city control within 60 days. The council passed it as revised on September 15th.

S6.headline: Same pole. Two councils.
labels: LEANDER Stopped September 4th. The city says it was "in response to community concerns."
COLLEGE STATION Kept, 4 to 2. "You can't afford the number of cops it would take," says its police chief.
strings: Stopped September 4th. The city says it was "in response to community concerns."
Kept, 4 to 2. "You can't afford the number of cops it would take," says its police chief.

S7.headline: Kyle kept its contract, 6 to 1.
S7.body: Its $205,000 grant for 2026 had not arrived, the Tribune reported. Of that, $80,000 would help pay for 32 Flock cameras.
strings: Its $205,000 grant for 2026 had not arrived, the Tribune reported. Of that, $80,000 would help pay for 32 Flock cameras.

S8.headline: Laredo will ask its voters.
S8.body: Its council voted 7 to 2 for a nonbinding referendum in May on spending $1 million a year to keep 165 cameras.
strings: Its council voted 7 to 2 for a nonbinding referendum in May on spending $1 million a year to keep 165 cameras.

S9.headline: League City votes next.
S9.body: Its voters answer a nonbinding question on November 3rd. Laredo's council voted 7 to 2 to ask its own in May.
strings: Its voters answer a nonbinding question on November 3rd. Laredo's council voted 7 to 2 to ask its own in May.
